To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the NMDAR 3-(2-Carboxypiperaziny-4-yl)-Propyl-1-Phosphonic Acid (CPP) binding site in the cerebral cortex is modified in a graded manner during hypoxia, and that the degree is correlated with the degree of cerebral hypoxia.
the NMDAR CPP binding site is modified in a dose-dependent fashion by hypoxia and is coupled to a decrease in brain cell PCr and an increase in conjugation of brain membrane fatty acids.
hypoxia induced modifications of the NMDAR CPP high-affinity binding sites are coupled to the degree of brain cell energy metabolism decline and lipid peroxidation increase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of graded hypoxemia on the high affinity CPP site of the N-methyl D-aspartate (NDMA) receptor in the cerebral cortices of newborn piglets.
understanding the mechanism of hypoxia-induced neuronal injury.
the effects of hypoxia on cerebral cortical NMDA receptor function and the relationship to brain cell energy metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hypoxia induces a progressive modification in NMDA receptor binding sites that are coupled to a gradual decline in brain cell energy status.
hypoxia causes a modification of the N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor 3-(carboxypiperazone-4-yl)-propyl-1- phosphonic acid (CPP)-binding site in newborn piglet cerebral cortex.
there is a correlation between the degree of modification of the N-Methyl-D-Aspartate receptor and cerebral energy metabolism and lipid peroxidation during graded hypoxia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NMDAR is modified during hypoxic ischemia in a dose dependent manner and that modification is coupled with a progressive decrease in brain cell metabolic activity.

hypoxia induces a decrease in the number of NMDA receptors in the cerebral cortex, and that the degree to which this occurs depends on the severity of the hypoxia and the degree of energy depletion and lipid peroxidation that occurs in the brain.
hypoxia causes a progressive alteration in the NMDA binding site and this alteration may be mediated by changes in cellular energy metabolism and lipid peroxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NMDAR is modified by hypoxia and this modification is coupled to changes in brain cell metabolism and lipid peroxidation.
the NMDAR is a potential therapeutic target for neonatal brain injury.
the NMDAR is modified by graded hypoxia in a manner that correlates with the degree of hypoxia-induced brain injury.
